correctness.rationale: For connected X and a nontrivial G-character chi with continuous equivariant p:X->S¹, any nullhomotopic equivariant h yields a real lift u of p∘h. Its increments u(xg)-u(x) lie in one integer coset as x varies, hence are constant on connected X. Evaluating at fixed x gives a continuous homomorphism a:G->(R,+), trivial because G is compact, contradicting chi. A character of compact abelian K separates every nonidentity g in G, and restriction supplies p. Translation is free; the cited join/nullhomotopy correspondence then forbids K*G->K. The coordinate embedding Z_p into product of S¹ via p^k residue roots is continuous, injective and closed, while the full product is connected. Checked all quantifiers; X need not be locally simply connected because the lift arises from a homotopy. The only unverified imported result is the exact form of the published general join correspondence.

value.rationale: The same Z_p group can act freely on connected compact product spaces with opposite join outcomes. A nontrivial circle-valued eigenfunction gives a transparent obstruction for all nontrivial closed translation subgroups of arbitrary connected compact abelian K; it illuminates the action-versus-group boundary in a current Borsuk–Ulam problem, not a toy calculation.
